sentences.zh: 傅玄

translations.literal: Fu Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan is the subject of this biography.

sentences.zh: 傅玄，字休奕，北地泥陽人也。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan, courtesy name Xiuyi, was a native of Niyang in Beidi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan, whose courtesy name was Xiuyi, came from Niyang in Beidi.

sentences.zh: 祖燮，漢漢陽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fu Xie served as Administrator of Hanyang under the Han.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fu Xie had been Han Administrator of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 父幹，魏扶風太守。

translations.literal: His father Fu Gan was Administrator of Fufeng under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fu Gan served Wei as Administrator of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 玄少孤貧，博學善屬文，解鐘律。

translations.literal: Xuan was orphaned young and poor; he was broadly learned, skilled at composing texts, and understood bell-tones and musical pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in youth, Fu Xuan nevertheless mastered a wide range of learning, wrote well, and understood musical theory.

sentences.zh: 性剛勁亮直，不能容人之短。

translations.literal: By nature he was rigid, forceful, candid, and upright, and could not tolerate others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: He was blunt and uncompromising by temperament and had little patience for others' shortcomings.

sentences.zh: 郡上計吏再舉孝廉，太尉辟，皆不就。

translations.literal: The commandery forwarding clerk twice nominated him Filially Pious and Incorrupt; the Grand Commandant summoned him; he accepted none of these.
translations.idiomatic: Twice the commandery recommended him as Filially Pious and Incorrupt, and the Grand Commandant offered him appointment, but he declined every summons.

sentences.zh: 州舉秀才，除郎中，與東海繆施俱以時譽選入著作，撰集《魏書》。

translations.literal: The province nominated him Flourishing Talent; he was appointed Gentleman of the Palace, and together with Mu Shi of Donghai he was selected by contemporary reputation to enter the Editorial Service and compile the 《Wei shu》.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as a provincial "flourishing talent," he received a Gentleman's post and, alongside Mu Shi of Donghai—both men enjoying contemporary esteem—was drafted into the editorial office to help compile the 《Wei shu》.

sentences.zh: 後參安東、衛軍軍事，轉溫令，再遷弘農太守，領典農校尉。

translations.literal: Later he served as adviser on military affairs for the General Who Guards the East and the Guards Army; he was transferred to magistrate of Wen, twice promoted to Administrator of Hongnong, and concurrent Colonel Director of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to staff the headquarters of the Guard-East and Guards armies, became magistrate of Wen, rose twice to Administrator of Hongnong, and held the concurrent post of agriculture intendant.

sentences.zh: 所居稱職，數上書陳便宜，多所匡正。

translations.literal: In every post he was deemed competent; he repeatedly submitted memorials setting forth expedient measures and corrected many abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he earned a reputation for competence; he often memorialized with practical proposals and helped set policy right.

sentences.zh: 五等建，封鶉觚男。

translations.literal: When the five ranks were established, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Chungu.
translations.idiomatic: After the five-tier noble hierarchy was instituted, he received the barony of Chungu.

sentences.zh: 武帝為晉王，以玄為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was Prince of Jin, he appointed Xuan Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: While still Prince of Jin, the future Emperor Wu named Fu Xuan a Regular Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，進爵為子，加附馬都尉。

translations.literal: When the abdication occurred, his noble rank was advanced to viscount and he was additionally given the title Chief Clerk of the Household of the Principal Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jin dynastic transition his fief was raised to viscount's rank and he was also appointed chief steward attached to the imperial son-in-law's household.

sentences.zh: 帝初即位，廣納直言，開不諱之路，玄及散騎常侍皇甫陶共掌諫職。

translations.literal: When the emperor first ascended the throne, he broadly welcomed straightforward speech and opened a path where nothing need be concealed; Xuan together with Regular Palace Attendant Huangfu Tao jointly performed remonstrance duties.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his reign the emperor encouraged blunt counsel and welcomed criticism without reprisal; Fu Xuan and Huangfu Tao, both Regular Palace Attendants, shared responsibility for remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 玄上疏曰：「臣聞先王之臨天下也，明其大教，長其義節。

translations.literal: Xuan submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that when the kings of old faced All-under-Heaven, they clarified their great instruction and lengthened righteousness and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan presented a memorial: "I have read that the ancient kings, in ruling the realm, made clear the great moral teaching and nurtured a sense of duty and restraint.

sentences.zh: 道化隆于上，清議行於下，上下相奉，人懷義心。

translations.literal: The transforming power of the Way flourished above and pure discussion ran below; above and below upheld one another and every person cherished righteous intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Way's transforming influence flourished at court while honest opinion held sway in society; rulers and subjects reinforced each other until righteousness shaped every heart.

sentences.zh: 亡秦蕩滅先王之制，以法術相禦，而義心亡矣。

translations.literal: The perished Qin swept away the institutions of the former kings, employed laws and techniques to control one another, and righteous intent perished.
translations.idiomatic: The doomed Qin erased the old kings' institutions, ruled through naked legalism and administrative tricks, and thereby killed the moral conscience of the age.

sentences.zh: 近者魏武好法術，而天下貴刑名；

translations.literal: In recent times Emperor Wu of Wei favored laws and techniques, and All-under-Heaven esteemed penal names.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago Cao Cao favored Legalist methods, and the empire elevated harsh law-and-punishment doctrines.

sentences.zh: 魏文慕通達，而天下賤守節。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei admired facility and comprehension, and All-under-Heaven despised maintaining integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi admired clever versatility, and the world came to scorn steadfast moral principle.

sentences.zh: 其後綱維不攝，而虛無放誕之論盈於朝野，使天下無復清議，而亡秦之病復發於今。

translations.literal: Afterward the guiding cords were not gathered in, and discourse on emptiness and unruly license filled court and countryside, causing All-under-Heaven no longer to have pure discussion, and the illness of the perished Qin to break out again in the present.
translations.idiomatic: Later the moral framework collapsed; talk of voidness and reckless abandon flooded court and country until honest public judgment vanished—exactly the sickness that had destroyed Qin was appearing again.

sentences.zh: 陛下聖德，龍興受禪，弘堯、舜之化，開正直之路，體夏禹之至儉，綜殷周之典文，臣詠歎而已，將又奚言！

translations.literal: Your Majesty's sagely virtue, arising as a dragon and receiving the abdication, expands the transformation of Yao and Shun, opens the road of integrity, embodies the utmost frugality of Yu of Xia, and synthesizes the canonical texts of Yin and Zhou—your servant merely sings praise; what more could he say!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty received the mandate in a dragon ascent of sacred virtue; you extend the humane governance of Yao and Shun, welcome honest counsel, emulate Yu's austerity, and draw on the classical heritage of Shang and Zhou—I can only marvel aloud; what is left for me to add!

sentences.zh: 惟未舉清遠有禮之臣，以敦風節；

translations.literal: Only you have not yet promoted pure, distant, and courteous ministers so as to thicken moral integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Only one thing still awaits: raising up ministers who are lucid in judgment, aloof from vulgarity, and punctilious in ritual, so as to shore up public virtue.

sentences.zh: 未退虛鄙，以懲不恪，臣是以猶敢有言。

translations.literal: You have not yet dismissed the hollow and base so as to punish lack of reverence—therefore your servant still dares to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Nor have hollow and contemptible men yet been cleared away to reprimand slack conduct—which is why I still presume to speak.

sentences.zh: 」詔報曰：「舉清遠有禮之臣者，此尤今之要也。

translations.literal: " An edict replied: "Promoting pure, distant, and courteous ministers—this is especially today's urgent need.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied by edict: "Elevating principled, refined ministers is precisely what matters most now."

sentences.zh: 」乃使玄草詔進之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered Xuan to draft an edict and advance it.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Fu Xuan draft the edict for promulgation.

sentences.zh: 玄復上疏曰：

translations.literal: Xuan again submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝下詔曰：「二常侍懇懇於所論，可謂乃心欲佐益時事者也。

translations.literal: When the document was presented, the emperor issued an edict saying: "The two Regular Attendants have earnestly labored over what they argue—this may be called giving their hearts to wish to assist and benefit current affairs."
translations.idiomatic: After reading the memorial, the emperor proclaimed: "These two Regular Attendants have argued their case with sincere perseverance; plainly they mean to help steady the times."

sentences.zh: 而主者率以常制裁之，豈得不使發憤耶！

translations.literal: Yet those in charge invariably restrain them by routine regulations—how could this not make them burst with indignation!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the responsible offices habitually tie them up in bureaucratic routine—small wonder they boil with frustration!

sentences.zh: 二常侍所論，或舉其大較而未備其條目，亦可便令作之，然後主者八坐廣共研精。

translations.literal: What the two Regular Attendants argue—perhaps they set forth the general outline but have not completed the articles—it is also permissible immediately to order them to compose these; afterward let those in charge and the eight seated ministers broadly join in refining them.
translations.idiomatic: Their proposals may state the broad principles without every procedural detail; still, let them draft concrete provisions, after which the department heads and the senior ministers can polish them together.

sentences.zh: 凡關言於人主，人臣之所至難。

translations.literal: In general, addressing speech to the sovereign is what is hardest for a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking truth to the throne is among the hardest duties a subject faces.

sentences.zh: 而人主若不能虛心聽納，自古忠臣直士之所慷慨，至使杜口結舌。

translations.literal: And if the sovereign cannot empty his mind and listen and accept, since antiquity loyal ministers and upright gentlemen have thereby sighed with feeling, even to the point of sealing their mouths and binding their tongues.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler refuses open-minded counsel, loyal officials have always felt blocked and bitter—until they simply fall silent.

sentences.zh: 每念於此，未嘗不歎息也。

translations.literal: Whenever I reflect on this, I have never failed to sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I think of it, I cannot help sighing.

sentences.zh: 故前詔敢有直言，勿有所距，庶幾得以發懞補過，獲保高位。

translations.literal: Therefore the prior edict said: dare to have straightforward speech; let nothing be refused—hopefully thereby to bring forth sincere counsel and remedy faults, and preserve high position.
translations.idiomatic: Hence my earlier order encouraged blunt speech and forbade brushing criticism aside—so that frank words might expose faults and worthy men keep their posts.

sentences.zh: 苟言有偏善，情在忠益，雖文辭有謬誤，言語有失得，皆當曠然恕之。

translations.literal: If speech has partial goodness and the intention lies in loyalty and benefit, though there be errors in literary phrasing and gains and losses in wording, all should be broadly forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: Where advice is partly sound and the motive is loyal concern, slipshod phrasing or infelicitous wording ought all to be forgiven outright.

sentences.zh: 古人猶不拒誹謗，況皆善意在可採錄乎！

translations.literal: The ancients still did not reject slander—how much more when all good intentions are worth adopting and recording!
translations.idiomatic: Even antiquity did not suppress bitter criticism—much less should we ignore counsel offered in good faith!

sentences.zh: 近者孔晁、綦毋龢皆案以輕慢之罪，所以皆原，欲使四海知區區之朝無諱言之忌也。

translations.literal: Recently Kong Chao and Qiwu He were both prosecuted on charges of levity and disrespect; the reason they were all pardoned was to let the Four Seas know this humble court has no taboo against speaking out.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chao and Qiwu He were lately charged with disrespect; I pardoned them deliberately, so the empire would see that this court does not punish plain speech.

sentences.zh: 」俄遷侍中。

translations.literal: " Soon he was promoted Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Fu Xuan was promoted to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，玄進皇甫陶，及入而抵，玄以事與陶爭，言喧嘩，為有司所奏，二人竟坐免官。

translations.literal: Earlier Xuan had recommended Huangfu Tao; when Tao entered office they clashed; Xuan quarreled with Tao over affairs, their words noisy and clamorous; they were memorialized by the relevant authorities, and both men ended up stripped of office for it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan had once recommended Huangfu Tao; once Tao arrived at court they repeatedly crossed swords over policy until their shouting drew a formal impeachment, and both lost their posts.

sentences.zh: ，以為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Imperial Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the court named him Imperial Clerk, chief of the censorial bureau.

sentences.zh: 時頗有水旱之災，玄復上疏曰：

translations.literal: At that time there were rather frequent flood and drought disasters; Xuan again submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Floods and droughts had become frequent; Fu Xuan again memorialized:

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「得所陳便宜，言農事得失及水官興廢，又安邊禦胡政事寬猛之宜，申省周備，一二具之，此誠為國大本，當今急務也。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Having obtained what you memorialize as expedient, speaking of agriculture's gains and losses and of water offices' establishment and abolition, also of securing the borders and resisting the Hu and the fitting balance of relaxed and stern governance—you have laid it out thoroughly and completely, item by item; this is truly the great foundation of the state and the urgent task of the moment.
translations.idiomatic: The court replied: "Your memorial covers farming policy, irrigation administration, frontier defense against the Hu, and when government should be tight or lenient—you have spelled everything out with rare thoroughness. These are precisely the state's foundations and today's pressing priorities."

sentences.zh: 如所論皆善，深知乃心，廣思諸宜，動靜以聞也。」

translations.literal: If what you argue is all good, we deeply know your mind; broadly ponder every expedient and report movement and stillness."
translations.idiomatic: Your proposals are sound; I understand your intent well—think through further measures as events unfold and keep me informed.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷太僕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was transferred to Grand Coachman.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the reign he was promoted to Grand Coachman.

sentences.zh: 時比年不登，羌胡擾邊，詔公卿會議。

translations.literal: At that time year after year the harvests did not ripen; the Qiang and Hu disturbed the borders; an edict ordered the dukes and ministers to convene in conference.
translations.idiomatic: Harvests failed year after year while Qiang and Hu raiders harried the frontier; the emperor ordered a joint council of high officials.

sentences.zh: 玄應對所問，陳事切直，雖不盡施行，而常見優容。

translations.literal: Xuan answered what was asked; he stated affairs bluntly and directly; though not everything was implemented, he was constantly treated with indulgent tolerance.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan answered forthrightly; though not every suggestion was adopted, the throne consistently indulged him.

sentences.zh: 轉司隸校尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Metropolitan Governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Metropolitan Governor, that is, Colonel Director of Retainers.

sentences.zh: 獻皇后崩于弘訓宮，設喪位。

translations.literal: Empress Xian died in Hongxun Palace; mourning stations were set up.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xian died at Hongxun Palace, mourning arrangements were established.

sentences.zh: 舊制，司隸於端門外坐，在諸卿上，絕席。

translations.literal: According to old regulations, the Metropolitan Governor sat outside the Duan Gate, above the various ministers, with a separate mat.
translations.idiomatic: By longstanding rule the Metropolitan Governor took a seat outside the Duan Gate above the ministers, on his own dais.

sentences.zh: 其入殿，按本品秩在諸卿下，以次坐，不絕席。

translations.literal: When entering the palace hall, according to his nominal rank and grade he was below the various ministers, seated in proper order without a separate mat.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the hall, however, his statutory rank placed him below the ministers in the seating order, without a separate mat.

sentences.zh: 而謁者以弘訓宮為殿內，制玄位在卿下。

translations.literal: But the herald considered Hongxun Palace as inside the palace; the regulation placed Xuan's position below the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The protocol officers treated Hongxun Palace as interior space and assigned Fu Xuan a seat below the ministers.

sentences.zh: 玄恚怒，厲聲色而責謁者。

translations.literal: Xuan was furious and harshly rebuked the herald with stern voice and expression.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan lost his temper and berated the herald loudly.

sentences.zh: 謁者妄稱尚書所處，玄對百僚而罵尚書以下。

translations.literal: The herald falsely claimed it was what the Masters of Writing had determined; Xuan in front of the hundred officials reviled the Masters of Writing and those below.
translations.idiomatic: The herald falsely blamed the Secretariat; Fu Xuan then denounced the Secretariat before the entire assembly.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞庾純奏玄不敬，玄又自表不以實，坐免官。

translations.literal: Imperial Clerk Yu Chun memorialized that Xuan had been disrespectful; Xuan moreover submitted a self-report that did not accord with facts; he was stripped of office for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun impeached him for disrespect; Fu Xuan's defense misrepresented the facts, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 然玄天性峻急，不能有所容；

translations.literal: However Xuan by nature was severe and hasty and could not accommodate anything.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Fu Xuan was irascible by nature and tolerated no opposition.

sentences.zh: 每有奏劾，或值日暮，捧白簡，整簪帶，竦踴不寐，坐而待旦。

translations.literal: Whenever he had a memorial impeachment, sometimes encountering dusk, he would hold the white tablet, straighten hairpin and belt, stand rigidly unable to sleep, sit and await dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he drafted an impeachment—even at dusk—he would clutch his ivory impeachment slip, straighten his hat and sash, and sit rigidly awake until dawn.

sentences.zh: 於是貴遊懾伏，臺閣生風。

translations.literal: Thereupon the noble wanderers were awed into submission, and the terraces and pavilions generated wind.
translations.idiomatic: The great families quailed before him, and a chill discipline seemed to sweep the ministries.

sentences.zh: 尋卒于家，時年六十二，諡曰剛。

translations.literal: Soon he died at home, aged sixty-two; his posthumous title was Gang.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home not long after, at sixty-two, with the posthumous epithet "Rigid."

sentences.zh: 玄少時避難於河內，專心誦學，後雖顯貴，而著述不廢。

translations.literal: When young Xuan fled disaster to Henei and devoted himself to recitation and study; later although he became eminent and noble, he did not abandon writing.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had taken refuge in Henei and immersed himself in scholarship; even after rising to high rank he never stopped writing.

sentences.zh: 撰論經國九流及三史故事，評斷得失，各為區例，名為《傅子》，為內、外、中篇，凡有四部、六錄，合百四十首，數十萬言，並文集百餘卷行於世。

translations.literal: He composed treatises on ordering the state, the nine currents, and precedents from the three histories, judging gains and losses, each with sectional examples, titled the 《Fu zi》, comprising inner, outer, and middle sections—in all four divisions, six registers, totaling one hundred forty pieces and several hundred thousand characters, together with a literary collection of over one hundred fascicles circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote discourses on statecraft, the nine intellectual traditions, and institutional precedents drawn from the standard histories, weighing right and wrong in organized chapters collected as the 《Fu zi》—inner, outer, and central portions totaling four parts, six registers, one hundred forty essays, and hundreds of thousands of characters—alongside another literary corpus of well over a hundred scrolls that circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 玄初作內篇成，子咸以示司空王沈。

translations.literal: When Xuan first finished the inner sections, his son Xian showed them to Minister of Works Wang Shen.
translations.idiomatic: When he completed the inner books of the 《Fu zi》, his son Fu Xian showed them to Wang Shen, the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 沈與玄書曰：「省足下所著書，言富理濟，經綸政體，存重儒教，足以塞楊、墨之流遁，齊孫、孟于往代。

translations.literal: Shen wrote to Xuan saying: "I have examined what you have composed; the words are rich and the principles aid governance; it arrays the political body and preserves and esteems Confucian teaching—sufficient to block the evasions of Yang Zhu and Mozi, and rank Sun Qing and Mencius with former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen wrote: "I have read your work: the argument is ample and the doctrine serves governance; it maps the structures of government and upholds Confucian teaching—enough to cut off Yangist and Mohist evasions and set Xunzi and Mencius beside the worthies of antiquity."

sentences.zh: 每開卷，未嘗不歎息也。

translations.literal: Whenever I open the fascicle, I have never failed to sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Every time I open it I find myself sighing in admiration.

sentences.zh: 『不見賈生，自以過之，乃今不及』，信矣！」

translations.literal: "Not seeing Jia Yi, I thought I surpassed him—now I do not reach him"—how true!"
translations.idiomatic: "Until I saw Jia Yi I fancied myself his better—now I know I fall short." How true!

sentences.zh: 其後追封清泉侯。

translations.literal: Afterward he was posthumously enfeoffed Marquis of Qingquan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posthumously invested as Marquis of Qingquan.

sentences.zh: 子咸嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu Xian inherited the title.

translations.literal: The received lemma contains only an equals sign; there is no lexical sentence.
translations.idiomatic: No readable Chinese clause appears here—likely a transcription artifact.

sentences.zh: 子咸

translations.literal: Son Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan's son: Fu Xian.

sentences.zh: =咸字長虞，剛簡有大節。

translations.literal: Xian's courtesy name was Changyu; he was stern and spare and had great integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian, courtesy name Changyu, combined austerity with high moral seriousness.

sentences.zh: 風格峻整，識性明悟，疾惡如仇，推賢樂善，常慕季文子、仲山甫之志。

translations.literal: His manner was sternly ordered; his knowing nature was bright and comprehending; he hated evil as if an enemy; he promoted the worthy and delighted in goodness; he constantly admired the aims of Ji Wenzi and Zhong Shanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and disciplined in deportment, acute in judgment, he loathed wickedness as personally as an enemy while lifting worthy men and rejoicing in the good—always modeling himself on Ji Wenzi and Zhong Shanfu.

sentences.zh: 好屬文論，雖綺麗不足，而言成規鑒。

translations.literal: He liked composing literary essays; although ornate splendor was insufficient, his words formed models and mirrors.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to write essays; they lacked ornament but served as clear standards for readers.

sentences.zh: 潁川庾純常歎曰：「長虞之文近乎詩人之作矣！」

translations.literal: Yu Chun of Yingchuan often sighed saying: "Changyu's writings are close to the productions of the poets!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun of Yingchuan used to exclaim, "Changyu writes almost like a poet!"

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，襲父爵，拜太子洗馬，累遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianning era, he inherited his father's noble rank, was appointed Groom for the Heir Apparent, and repeatedly promoted to Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianning he succeeded to his father's title, entered the heir apparent's household as attendant groom, and rose through several posts to Assistant Director of the right bureau of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 出為冀州刺史，繼母杜氏不肯隨咸之官，自表解職。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Ji Province; his stepmother the Lady Du was unwilling to follow Xian to his post; he personally memorialized to resign office.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as Inspector of Ji, he resigned because his stepmother Lady Du refused to accompany him to his province.

sentences.zh: 三旬之間，遷司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Within thirty days he was promoted Left Senior Clerk of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was appointed senior clerk on the Minister of Education's staff.

sentences.zh: 時帝留心政事，詔訪朝臣政之損益。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor attended to administrative affairs and issued an edict inquiring of court ministers about gains and losses in governance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply engaged in government and ordered court officials to comment on what helped or harmed the administration.

sentences.zh: 咸上言曰：「陛下處至尊之位，而修布衣之事，親覽萬機，勞心日昃。

translations.literal: Xian submitted words saying: "Your Majesty occupies the most honored position yet cultivates common-cloth affairs; personally reviewing the myriad threads, you toil in heart until the sun slants.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian wrote: "Though seated on the throne you live like a diligent commoner, personally steering every policy until sunset.

sentences.zh: 在昔帝王，躬自菲薄，以利天下，未有逾陛下也。

translations.literal: Among emperors and kings of old who personally practiced austerity to benefit All-under-Heaven, none has surpassed Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient sovereigns who tightened their own belts for the realm's sake never outdid you.

sentences.zh: 然泰始開元以暨於今，十有五年矣。

translations.literal: Yet from the Taishi founding opening until now, there have been fifteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fifteen years have passed since the Taishi founding.

sentences.zh: 而軍國未豐，百姓不贍，一歲不登便有菜色者，誠由官眾事殷，復除猥濫，蠶食者多而親農者少也。

translations.literal: Yet army and state are not abundant; the hundred surnames are not sufficient; if one year does not ripen there are persons with the color of greens—truly because officials are many and affairs numerous, exemptions are reckless and excessive, those who nibble away are many while those who personally farm are few.
translations.idiomatic: Yet neither treasury nor people thrives; a single bad harvest brings hollow cheeks everywhere—because offices multiply, tax exemptions are handed out indiscriminately, parasites devour resources, and too few till the soil themselves.

sentences.zh: 臣以頑疏，謬忝近職，每見聖詔以百姓饑饉為慮，無能雲補，伏用慚恧，敢不自竭，以對天問。

translations.literal: Your servant by dullness and looseness has wrongly occupied a nearby post; whenever he sees sacred edicts taking the hundred surnames' famine as worry, lacking ability to add a cloud's worth of help, he hides his face in shame; how dare he not exhaust himself to answer Heaven's question.
translations.idiomatic: Coarse and obscure as I am, I yet hold a place near the throne; whenever Your Majesty's edicts voice alarm over popular hunger I feel useless shame—so I dare reply with everything I can offer.

sentences.zh: 舊都督有四，今並監軍，乃盈於十。

translations.literal: Formerly there were four area commanders; now together with army supervisors they exceed ten.
translations.idiomatic: We once had four regional commanders; with supervisory postings thrown in they now number over ten.

sentences.zh: 夏禹敷土，分為九州，今之刺史，幾向一倍。

translations.literal: Yu of Xia spread the soil and divided into nine provinces; today's provincial governors nearly approach double.
translations.idiomatic: Yu mapped the realm into nine provinces; we now maintain nearly twice as many provincial inspectors.

sentences.zh: 戶口比漢十分之一，而置郡縣更多。

translations.literal: Household registration compared to Han is one tenth, yet established commanderies and counties are even more.
translations.idiomatic: Registered households are barely a tenth of Han levels, yet we maintain even more counties and commanderies.

sentences.zh: 空校牙門，無益宿衛，而虛立軍府，動有百數。

translations.literal: Empty camps and headquarters gates bring no benefit to palace guard; yet hollow army headquarters are established, often reaching the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Hollow garrison posts do nothing for palace security while phantom army yamen sprawl by the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 五等諸侯，復坐置官屬。

translations.literal: The feudal lords of the five ranks again sit and establish official subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Each noble of the five ranks runs a full personal bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 諸所寵給，皆生於百姓。

translations.literal: All that is favored and supplied is born from the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Every stipend they receive comes straight from the people.

sentences.zh: 一夫不農，有受其饑，今之不農，不可勝計。

translations.literal: If one husband does not farm, there are those who receive hunger from it; today's non-farmers cannot be reckoned.
translations.idiomatic: Classical wisdom says when one man leaves the plough someone goes hungry—today innumerable hands never touch the soil.

sentences.zh: 縱使五稼普收，僅足相接；

translations.literal: Even supposing the five grains universally ripen, it barely suffices to link together.
translations.idiomatic: Even a bumper harvest across every crop would scarcely keep pace.

sentences.zh: 暫有災患，便不繼贍。

translations.literal: Temporarily having disaster and calamity, then there is no continuation of provision.
translations.idiomatic: The slightest disaster breaks the chain of supply.

sentences.zh: 以為當今之急，先並官省事，靜事息役，上下用心，惟農是務也。」

translations.literal: Your servant considers that today's urgency is first to merge offices and reduce affairs, quiet affairs and cease corvée; above and below apply heart; only agriculture is the task."
translations.idiomatic: The pressing need is to consolidate offices, cut busywork, end needless labor service, and focus every level of government on farming alone."

sentences.zh: 咸在位多所執正。

translations.literal: While in office Xian often upheld rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: In office Fu Xian repeatedly insisted on proper procedure.

sentences.zh: 豫州大中正夏侯駿上言，魯國小中正、司空司馬孔毓，四移病所，不能接賓，求以尚書郎曹馥代毓，旬日復上毓為中正。

translations.literal: The Yu Province Grand Selector Xiahou Jun memorialized that Kong Yu, Minor Selector of Lu and Palace Clerk to the Minister of Works, had shifted his sick quarters four times and could not receive guests, requesting that Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Cao Fu replace Yu; ten days later he again nominated Yu as Selector.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Province's chief neutral evaluator Xiahou Jun reported that Kong Yu—Lu's junior evaluator and an aide at the Ministry of Works—had relocated his sickbed four times and could no longer entertain callers, and sought to swap in Cao Fu—then within ten days tried to put Kong Yu back in office.

sentences.zh: 司徒三卻，駿故據正。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education thrice refused; Jun therefore held to rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education rejected the paperwork three times, yet Xiahou Jun stubbornly pressed his point.

sentences.zh: 咸以駿與奪惟意，乃奏免駿大中正。

translations.literal: Xian considered that Jun's granting and taking followed mere whim; therefore he memorialized to dismiss Jun from Grand Selector.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian believed Xiahou Jun was manipulating appointments on whim and impeached him out of the chief evaluator post.

sentences.zh: 司徒魏舒，駿之姻屬，屢卻不署，咸據正甚苦。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Wei Shu was Jun's marriage relative; repeatedly refusing he would not sign; Xian holding to rectitude was very bitter.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wei Shu, Xiahou Jun's kinsman by marriage, repeatedly blocked the paperwork; Fu Xian fought bitterly to uphold protocol.

sentences.zh: 舒終不從，咸遂獨上。

translations.literal: Shu in the end did not comply; Xian therefore alone advanced the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu never yielded, so Fu Xian filed the impeachment unilaterally.

sentences.zh: 舒奏咸激訕不直，詔轉咸為車騎司馬。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized that Xian was provocative and slanderous and not upright; an edict transferred Xian to Army Supervisor for the Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu accused Fu Xian of malicious insinuation; the court reassigned him as carriage-and-cavalry army aide.

sentences.zh: 咸以世俗奢侈，又上書曰：「臣以為穀帛難生，而用之不節，無緣不匱。

translations.literal: Xian, considering worldly customs extravagant, again submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant considers that grain and silk are hard to produce, yet if use is not restrained, there is no reason they will not be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Troubled by lavish habits at court, Fu Xian wrote again: "Grain and silk do not come easily; spend without restraint and scarcity follows inevitably.

sentences.zh: 故先王之化天下，食肉衣帛，皆有其制。

translations.literal: Therefore when former kings transformed All-under-Heaven, eating meat and wearing silk each had its regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings regulated even meat-eating and silk-wearing so consumption matched produce.

sentences.zh: 竊謂奢侈之費，甚於天災。

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers that the expense of extravagance surpasses natural disasters.
translations.idiomatic: I believe wasteful luxury drains the realm more cruelly than flood or drought.

sentences.zh: 古者堯有茅茨，今之百姓競豐其屋。

translations.literal: In antiquity Yao had thatched roofs; today's commoners vie to enlarge their houses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yao lived beneath thatch; today ordinary families compete to build ever grander homes.

sentences.zh: 古者臣無玉食，今之賈豎皆厭粱肉。

translations.literal: In antiquity ministers did not eat "jade food"; today's merchants and peddlers all tire of fine millet and meat.
translations.idiomatic: Once even senior officials seldom tasted luxurious fare; now petty traders are surfeited with the best grain and meat.

sentences.zh: 古者后妃乃有殊飾，今之婢妾被服綾羅。

translations.literal: In antiquity only empresses and consorts wore exceptional ornaments; today's maids and concubines are clothed in damask and gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Finery once reserved for palace ladies now drapes slave girls and secondary wives.

sentences.zh: 古者大夫乃不徒行，今之賤隸乘輕驅肥。

translations.literal: In antiquity grandees did not walk alone on foot; today's mean slaves ride light carriages and drive fat horses.
translations.idiomatic: Men of rank once rode rather than walked; today low servants parade on sleek horses and in fast gigs.

sentences.zh: 古者人稠地狹而有儲蓄，由於節也；

translations.literal: In antiquity people were crowded on narrow land yet still saved grain—owing to restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient populations were dense and fields small, yet granaries stayed full because people lived frugally.

sentences.zh: 今者土廣人稀而患不足，由於奢也。

translations.literal: Today land is vast and population sparse yet we fret over shortage—owing to extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Now fields are wide and people few, yet want persists—because luxury wastes what plenty could supply.

sentences.zh: 欲時之儉，當詰其奢；

translations.literal: Desiring frugality for the age, one must call out extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: If we want thrift in our times, we must discipline excess wherever it appears.

sentences.zh: 奢不見詰，轉相高尚。

translations.literal: When extravagance is never challenged, people successively glorify it.
translations.idiomatic: Unchecked ostentation becomes a contest in conspicuous consumption.

sentences.zh: 昔毛玠為吏部尚書，時無敢好衣美食者。

translations.literal: Formerly Mao Jie served as Minister of Personnel; at that time no one dared fine clothes or rich food.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mao Jie's tenure at the Ministry of Personnel, nobody flaunted sumptuous dress or banquets.

sentences.zh: 魏武帝歎曰：『孤之法不如毛尚書。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei sighed: 'My laws do not equal Minister Mao.'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao once lamented that his own statutes fell short of Mao Jie's standards.

sentences.zh: 』令使諸部用心，各如毛玠，風俗之移，在不難矣。

translations.literal: 'Were every department to apply itself like Mao Jie, shifting customs would not be difficult.'
translations.idiomatic: Had each bureau worked with Mao Jie's discipline, reforming habits would have been easy.

sentences.zh: 」又議移縣獄於郡及二社應立，朝廷從之。

translations.literal: He also urged moving county prisons to the commandery level and erecting the twin soil altars; the court approved.
translations.idiomatic: His further proposals—to relocate county jails under commandery authority and establish the two soil altars—were adopted.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing on the left.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to left Assistant Director at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 惠帝即位，楊駿輔政。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui ascended the throne, Yang Jun directed government.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui's accession brought Yang Jun to power as regent.

sentences.zh: 咸言於駿曰：「事與世變，禮隨時宜，諒暗之不行尚矣。

translations.literal: Xian said to Jun: "Affairs alter with each age and ritual must suit the times; the strict mourning seclusion of old has long been impracticable.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian warned Yang Jun: "Institutions must evolve; the archaic ideal of total palatial seclusion during mourning no longer fits reality.

sentences.zh: 由世道彌薄，權不可假，故雖斬焉在疚，而躬覽萬機也。

translations.literal: Because moral customs grow ever thinner, authority cannot be lent away; therefore even while clad in mourning grief one must personally oversee the myriad affairs of state."
translations.idiomatic: In a decadent age power cannot be delegated, so sovereigns still handle every state paper even while wearing mourning.

sentences.zh: 逮至漢文，以天下體大，服重難久，遂制既葬而除。

translations.literal: Down to Emperor Wen of Han, because the empire was vast and heavy mourning could not be prolonged, he decreed shedding mourning garments once burial was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han shortened full mourning because the realm was too large to pause governance indefinitely; mourning dress ended with burial.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝雖大孝蒸蒸，亦從時釋服，制心喪三年，至於萬機之事，則有不遑。

translations.literal: Our dynastic founder Emperor Wu, though steeped in filial devotion, likewise followed the times in easing formal mourning while observing three years of heartfelt grief—yet even then state business allowed little respite.
translations.idiomatic: Even founding Emperor Wu, profoundly filial, adjusted outward mourning to circumstance while keeping three years of inward grief—yet still found government overwhelming.

sentences.zh: 今聖上欲委政於公，諒暗自居，此雖謙讓之心，而天下未以為善。

translations.literal: Now the sage sovereign wishes to place administration in your hands and himself observe mourning seclusion—however modest the intent, All-under-Heaven does not praise it.
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor means to leave affairs to you and withdraw in mourning; however humble that sounds, the empire does not welcome it.

sentences.zh: 天下未以為善者，以億兆顒顒，戴仰宸極，聽於冢宰，懼天光有蔽。

translations.literal: They disapprove because millions crane toward the throne; if they must listen only to a chief steward they fear the celestial radiance is obscured.
translations.idiomatic: People look to the throne itself; hearing only a regent's voice they worry that true imperial authority is hidden.

sentences.zh: 人心既已若此，而明公處之固未為易也。

translations.literal: With popular feeling already thus, your lordship's position is anything but easy.
translations.idiomatic: Given such sentiment, sir, your footing as regent remains precarious.

sentences.zh: 竊謂山陵之事既畢，明公當思隆替之宜。

translations.literal: Your servant privately believes that once the imperial tomb works are finished you should weigh what advances or imperils the state.
translations.idiomatic: Once the burial rites conclude, you must decide what truly stabilizes or endangers the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 周公聖人，猶不免謗。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou was a sage yet still suffered slander.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Duke of Zhou faced malicious gossip.

sentences.zh: 以此推之，周公之任既未易而處，況聖上春秋非成王之年乎！

translations.literal: From this one sees his burden was hard to bear—how much more when our sovereign is no longer a child like King Cheng!
translations.idiomatic: If regency taxed the Duke of Zhou, how much heavier is it when the emperor is no mere boy like King Cheng of Zhou?

sentences.zh: 得意忘言，言未易盡。

translations.literal: Once meaning is grasped words may be forgotten—yet words are never easy to exhaust.
translations.idiomatic: Insight transcends wording, yet language can never capture everything.

sentences.zh: 苟明公有以察其悾款，言豈在多。

translations.literal: If your lordship can perceive this earnest loyalty, eloquence need not be lengthy.
translations.idiomatic: If you recognize sincere loyalty, a few heartfelt sentences suffice.

sentences.zh: 」時司隸荀愷從兄喪，自表赴哀，詔聽之而未下，愷乃造駿。

translations.literal: " At that time Metropolitan Governor Xun Kai was mourning an elder cousin; he memorialized for leave and an edict approved but had not yet been issued when Kai presented himself at Jun's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Xun Kai, Metropolitan Governor, sought leave to mourn a cousin; imperial approval had not yet been promulgated when he hurried to Yang Jun's door.

sentences.zh: 咸因奏曰：「死喪之戚，兄弟孔懷。

translations.literal: Xian therefore memorialized: "The sorrow of death binds brothers closely.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian seized the occasion: "Funeral grief should unite kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 同堂亡隕，方在信宿，聖恩矜憫，聽使臨喪。

translations.literal: A cousin of the same lineage had just died; within two nights sacred kindness pitied him and permitted attendance at the rites.
translations.idiomatic: The cousin had barely lain two nights in death when imperial grace allowed Kai to join the mourning.

sentences.zh: 詔未下而便以行造，急諂媚之敬，無友于之情。

translations.literal: Yet before the edict arrived he hastened to pay court—eager flattery, not brotherly feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he scampered to your gate before the order appeared—a naked bid for favor, not familial duty.

sentences.zh: 宜加顯貶，以隆風教。

translations.literal: He should be publicly demoted to shore up moral instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Demote him visibly to teach the capital what integrity means.

sentences.zh: 」帝以駿管朝政，有詔不問，駿甚憚之。

translations.literal: " The emperor, because Jun controlled court affairs, ordered no inquiry; Jun nonetheless feared Xian deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor shielded Jun and refused an investigation, yet Jun grew terrified of Fu Xian.

sentences.zh: 咸復與駿箋諷切之，駿意稍折，漸以不平。

translations.literal: Xian again sent Jun pointed letters of remonstrance; Jun yielded slightly but nursed growing resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Further blunt notes from Fu Xian bent Yang Jun a little yet bred quiet bitterness.

sentences.zh: 由是欲出為京兆、弘農太守，駿甥李斌說駿，不宜斥出正人，乃止。

translations.literal: Jun therefore wished to post him out as Administrator of Jingzhao or Hongnong; Jun's nephew Li Bin argued that upright men must not be banished, so the plan stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun tried to exile him to Jingzhao or Hongnong until nephew Li Bin argued that expelling honest ministers would backfire.

sentences.zh: 駿弟濟素與咸善，與咸書曰：「江海之流混混，故能成其深廣也。

translations.literal: Jun's younger brother Ji, long friendly with Xian, wrote: "River and sea currents run turbid and vast—thus they achieve depth and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji, Jun's brother and Fu Xian's friend, wrote: "Great waters stay deep because they churn endlessly.

sentences.zh: 天下大器，非可稍了，而相觀每事欲了。

translations.literal: The empire is a vast vessel—not something finished in a moment—yet you watch each matter as if it could be settled at once.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is not a checklist to complete overnight, yet you treat every file as urgent.

sentences.zh: 生子癡，了官事，官事未易了也。

translations.literal: They say a foolish son "finishes" paperwork—yet paperwork is never truly finished.
translations.idiomatic: Proverbs mock the dullard who claims paperwork is "done"; government never ends.

sentences.zh: 了事正作癡，復為快耳！

translations.literal: Calling it finished is precisely folly—and mistaking folly for cleverness!
translations.idiomatic: Boasting that affairs are "settled" is self-delusion dressed up as savvy.

sentences.zh: 左丞總司天臺，維正八坐，此未易居。

translations.literal: The left Assistant Director oversees the celestial terrace and reins in the eight senior ministers—a seat few hold easily.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Director supervises the whole Secretariat and checks the eight chief ministers—not an easy chair.

sentences.zh: 以君盡性而處未易居之任，益不易也。

translations.literal: With your uncompromising nature filling so demanding a post the difficulty redoubles.
translations.idiomatic: Your blunt honesty makes an already perilous office harder still.

sentences.zh: 想慮破頭，故具有白。

translations.literal: Anxiety racks my mind; therefore I spell everything out plainly.
translations.idiomatic: I fret myself sick over you, so I lay every thought bare.

sentences.zh: 」咸答曰：「衛公-{云}-酒色之殺人，此甚於作直。

translations.literal: " Xian replied: "Lord Wei remarked that wine and women kill men faster than blunt counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian answered: "Lord Wei observed that dissipation kills faster than plain speech.

sentences.zh: 坐酒色死，人不為悔。

translations.literal: Men who die of wine and beds rarely repent.
translations.idiomatic: Those who perish from pleasure seldom regret the path.

sentences.zh: 逆畏以直致禍，此由心不直正，欲以苟且為明哲耳！

translations.literal: Shunning honesty for fear of disaster shows a heart that is not upright—it is cowardice mistaken for wisdom!
translations.idiomatic: Fearing frankness because it invites trouble reveals a crooked heart hiding behind "prudence."

sentences.zh: 自古以直致禍者，當自矯枉過直，或不忠允，欲以亢厲為聲，故致忿耳。

translations.literal: Those throughout history who suffered for bluntness usually overcorrected, or lacked loyal fairness, or sought reputation through harsh noise—thereby provoking wrath.
translations.idiomatic: Straight men punished in the past generally overshot, acted unfairly, or courted fame through shrill attacks—small wonder they angered others.

sentences.zh: 安有空空為忠益，而當見疾乎！

translations.literal: How could loyalty offered without ulterior motive deserve contempt!
translations.idiomatic: Pure loyalty meant for the common good should never earn hatred.

sentences.zh: 」居無何，駿誅。

translations.literal: " Before long Jun was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yang Jun died by execution.

sentences.zh: 咸轉為太子中庶子，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: Xian was transferred to Palace Gentleman Attendant of the heir apparent's household and promoted Imperial Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian moved to the heir apparent's inner staff and rose to Imperial Clerk.

sentences.zh: 時太宰、汝南王亮輔政，咸致書曰：

translations.literal: When Grand Tutor Sima Liang, Prince of Runan, directed government, Xian sent him a letter:
translations.idiomatic: Under Prince Liang of Runan as regent, Fu Xian wrote:

sentences.zh: 咸復以亮輔政專權，又諫曰：「楊駿有震主之威，委任親戚，此天下所以喧嘩。

translations.literal: Xian, judging Liang's regency autocratic, remonstrated again: "Yang Jun inspired awe that overshadowed the throne and stuffed offices with kin—that is why the realm erupted.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian warned that Yang Jun's faction had intimidated the boy emperor and packed posts with relatives, provoking uproar.

sentences.zh: 今之處重，宜反此失。

translations.literal: Occupying weighty office now, you must reverse that error.
translations.idiomatic: Power today demands the opposite approach.

sentences.zh: 謂宜靜默頤神，有大得失，乃維持之；

translations.literal: Withdraw in silence and nurture your spirit; intervene only when major right or wrong appears.
translations.idiomatic: Stay quiet, husband your strength, and act chiefly when sweeping issues arise.

sentences.zh: 自非大事，一皆抑遣。

translations.literal: Unless the matter is momentous, suppress and defer it.
translations.idiomatic: Leave lesser business aside.

sentences.zh: 比四造詣，及經過尊門，冠蓋車馬，填塞街衢，此之翕習，既宜弭息。

translations.literal: Lately you have paid four visits; passing your gate fills the streets with coaches—such habitual bustle ought to cease.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated trips past your mansion choke the avenues with carriages; end this theatrical traffic.

sentences.zh: 又夏侯長容奉使為先帝請命，祈禱無感，先帝崩背，宜自咎責，而自求請命之勞，而公以為少府。

translations.literal: Moreover Xiahou Changrong carried an embassy to prolong the late emperor's life; prayers failed and the sovereign died—he should blame himself, yet he boasts of that mission while you appoint him Palace Superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Jun (Changrong) prayed in vain for the late emperor's recovery yet parades that embassy as merit—while you reward him as Palace Superintendent.

sentences.zh: 私竊之論，雲長容則公之姻，故至於此。

translations.literal: Private rumor says Changrong is your in-law—hence the favor.
translations.idiomatic: Whispers attribute his promotion to marriage ties with you.

sentences.zh: 一犬吠形，群犬吠聲，懼於群吠，遂至叵聽也。

translations.literal: One dog barks at a shadow and the pack howls along; fearing the chorus you shut your ears.
translations.idiomatic: One stray rumor breeds a chorus of gossip; dreading noise you stop listening.

sentences.zh: 咸之為人，不能面從而有後言。

translations.literal: As to Xian's character—he cannot nod assent to your face then murmur behind your back.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot flatter you in person and carp in private.

sentences.zh: 嘗觸楊駿，幾為身禍；

translations.literal: Once he offended Yang Jun and nearly lost his life.
translations.idiomatic: I nearly died crossing Yang Jun.

sentences.zh: 況于殿下，而當有惜！

translations.literal: How much more toward Your Highness—and should he restrain himself!
translations.idiomatic: With you, sire, restraint would be dishonest.

sentences.zh: 往從駕，殿下見語：『卿不識韓非逆鱗之言耶，而欻摩天子逆鱗！

translations.literal: While attending the carriage Your Highness told him: "Have you not read Han Fei on stroking the ruler's inverted scales—yet you rashly brush the Son of Heaven's scales!
translations.idiomatic: You once reminded me of Han Fei's "inverted scales," yet I keep touching the dragon's throat.

sentences.zh: 』自知所陳，誠𬱃𬱃觸猛獸之須耳。

translations.literal: 'Your servant knows his petitions amounted to rashly tweaking a fierce beast's whiskers.'
translations.idiomatic: I know my words were like tweaking a tiger's whiskers.

sentences.zh: 所以敢言，庶殿下當識其不勝區區。

translations.literal: Yet he dares speak hoping Your Highness sees how sincerity overwhelms him.
translations.idiomatic: I speak anyway, trusting you recognize helpless earnestness.

sentences.zh: 前摩天子逆鱗，欲以盡忠；

translations.literal: Earlier he brushed the Son of Heaven's scales wishing to exhaust loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Before, I risked the emperor's wrath to prove loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今觸猛獸之須，非欲為惡，必將以此見恕。

translations.literal: Now he tweaks the fierce beast's whiskers—not from malice—and trusts he will be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: Now I tweak yours without malice and hope for patience.

sentences.zh: 」亮不納。

translations.literal: " Liang did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang ignored the advice.

sentences.zh: 長容者，夏侯駿也。

translations.literal: Changrong is Xiahou Jun.
translations.idiomatic: "Changrong" denotes Xiahou Jun.

sentences.zh: 會丙寅，詔群僚舉郡縣之職以補內官。

translations.literal: On the bingyin day an edict ordered officials to nominate commandery and county officers for interior posts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict on the bingyin day directed ministers to recommend local magistrates for capital appointments.

sentences.zh: 咸復上書曰：

translations.literal: Xian again submitted a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian memorialized again.

sentences.zh: 咸再為本郡中正，遭繼母憂去官。

translations.literal: Xian again served as Central Selector for his native commandery; mourning his stepmother he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He resumed hometown evaluator duties until stepmother's death forced resignation.

sentences.zh: 頃之，起以議郎，長兼司隸校尉。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was recalled as Consultant and concurrent Metropolitan Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned back as Consultant with concurrent Metropolitan Governor rank.

sentences.zh: 咸前後固辭，不聽，敕使者就拜，咸復送還印綬。

translations.literal: Xian declined repeatedly without success; an envoy was ordered to invest him at home yet he returned seal and ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He refused repeatedly; though an envoy tried to confer the seal at his door, he sent credentials back.

sentences.zh: 公車不通，催使攝職。

translations.literal: Memorial carriages could not pass—officials pressed him to assume duty.
translations.idiomatic: Petitions stalled while clerks hounded him to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 咸以身無兄弟，喪祭無主，重自陳乞，乃使於官舍設靈坐。

translations.literal: Because he had no brothers and lacked a chief mourner, he pleaded earnestly; the court allowed a spirit tablet in his official residence.
translations.idiomatic: Lacking brothers to manage sacrifices, he begged off until the throne allowed an ancestral seat inside his yamen.

sentences.zh: 咸又上表曰：「臣既駑弱，不勝重任。

translations.literal: Xian submitted another memorial: "Your servant is dull and weak and cannot shoulder heavy rank.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote again: "I am too feeble for such responsibility.

sentences.zh: 加在哀疚，假息日闋，陛下過意，授非所堪。

translations.literal: Added to mourning affliction his borrowed breath grows short; Your Majesty's favor assigns what he cannot sustain.
translations.idiomatic: Still deep in mourning I scarcely breathe; honors exceed my strength.

sentences.zh: 披露丹款，歸窮上聞，謬詔既往，終然無改。

translations.literal: He laid loyalty bare and appealed exhaustively; the mistaken edict stood unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: I poured out sincerity repeatedly yet the flawed appointment remained.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不能滅身以全禮教，義無靦然，虛忝隆寵。

translations.literal: Though unable to destroy himself for ritual's sake, righteousness forbids holding empty lofty favor.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot martyr myself for etiquette, yet honor bars me from clutching an undeserved title.

sentences.zh: 前受嚴詔，視事之日，私心自誓，隕越為報。

translations.literal: Earlier receiving stern edict, on the day he assumed office he privately swore to repay even by falling short.
translations.idiomatic: Forced earlier to obey, I privately vowed to serve though it cost me everything.

sentences.zh: 以貨賂流行，所宜深絕，切敕都官，以此為先。

translations.literal: Because bribery runs rampant what needs cutting off most urgently—he sternly ordered capital offices to tackle it first.
translations.idiomatic: Corruption spreads; I commanded metropolitan bureaus to attack graft first.

sentences.zh: 而經彌日月，未有所得。

translations.literal: Yet months passed with no results.
translations.idiomatic: Months yielded no catches.

sentences.zh: 斯由陛下有以獎厲，慮於愚戇，將必死系，故自掩檢以避其鋒耳。

translations.literal: This is because Your Majesty's signals reward timidity; clerks fear impeachment means certain death, so they hide evidence and dodge confrontation.
translations.idiomatic: Mixed messages reward caution; officials fear fatal punishment, hide proof, and dodge battle.

sentences.zh: 在職有日，既無赫然之舉，又不應弦垂翅，人誰復憚？

translations.literal: Holding office long yet achieving no splendid strike nor clipping wings—who would fear him?
translations.idiomatic: After long tenure I have seized no scalps nor clipped noble wings—why should anyone dread me?

sentences.zh: 故光祿大夫劉毅為司隸，聲震內外，遠近清肅。

translations.literal: Former Grand Counsellor Liu Yi as Metropolitan Governor shook inner and outer courts; far and near grew orderly.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi held the post awe ran through capital and provinces alike.

sentences.zh: 非徒毅有王臣匪躬之節，亦由所奏見從，威風得伸也。

translations.literal: Not only did Yi possess the integrity of a minister who forgets self—but memorials were heeded so awe could operate.
translations.idiomatic: His virtue mattered, yet success also came because the throne backed his indictments.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「但當思必應繩中理，威風日伸，何獨劉毅！」

translations.literal: " The edict replied: "Only consider applying law consistently—awe will grow daily; why envy Liu Yi alone!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered: "Enforce statutes even-handedly and authority grows—you need not imitate Liu Yi alone."

sentences.zh: 時朝廷寬弛，豪右放恣，交私請托，朝野溷淆。

translations.literal: At that time court discipline slackened; magnates ran wild, trading private favors until court and countryside blurred together.
translations.idiomatic: The court grew lax; great houses traded illicit favors until capital and countryside mingled in confusion.

sentences.zh: 咸奏免河南尹澹、左將軍倩、廷尉高光、兼河南尹何攀等，京都肅然，貴戚懾伏。

translations.literal: Xian memorialized to dismiss Administrator of Henan Tan, General of the Left Qian, Commandant of Justice Gao Guang, concurrent Administrator of Henan He Pan, and others—the capital grew orderly and noble kin trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian impeached Henan governor Tan, General Qian, Judge Gao Guang, concurrent governor He Pan, and others—silencing Luoyang's elite.

sentences.zh: 咸以「聖人久于其道，天下化成。

translations.literal: Xian argued: "When the sage long pursues his Way the realm completes its transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian quoted: "A sage who perseveres in the Way transforms the world.

sentences.zh: 是以唐、虞三載考績，九年黜陟。

translations.literal: Therefore Tang and Yu examined merit every three years and promoted or demoted every nine.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Tang and Yu graded officials triennially and adjusted ranks every nine years.

sentences.zh: 其在《周禮》，三年大比。

translations.literal: As stated in the Zhou li, there is a major review every three years.
translations.idiomatic: The classic Zhou li prescribes a thorough reckoning triennially.

sentences.zh: 孔子亦云，『三年有成』。

translations.literal: Confucius also said: 'In three years there is accomplishment.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius likewise said, "Within three years results appear."

sentences.zh: 而中間以來，長吏到官，未幾便遷，百姓困于無定，吏卒疲於送迎」。

translations.literal: Yet lately local magistrates barely arrive before transfer; commoners suffer endless instability and runners collapse escorting convoys."
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately magistrates rotate before locals settle; people suffer churn and escort corps tire endless farewells.

sentences.zh: 時僕射王戎兼吏部，咸奏：「戎備位臺輔，兼掌選舉，不能謐靜風俗，以凝庶績，至令人心傾動，開張浮競。

translations.literal: At that time Supervisor Wang Rong concurrently headed Personnel; Xian memorialized: "Rong fills a terrace post yet manages selection—he cannot quiet customs or consolidate achievements; hearts sway and vain rivalry spreads.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong, Vice-President of the Secretariat and personnel chief, failed to steady manners or consolidate governance—Fu Xian charged him with stirring hollow ambition.

sentences.zh: 中郎李重、李義不相匡正。

translations.literal: Gentlemen of the Household Li Chong and Li Yi failed to correct him.
translations.idiomatic: Household gentlemen Li Chong and Li Yi never checked him.

sentences.zh: 請免戎等官。

translations.literal: He asked that Rong and others be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian sought dismissal for Wang Rong and allies.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「政道之本，誠宜久於其職，咸奏是也。

translations.literal: " The edict said: "The root of government lies in long tenure—Xian's memorial is right.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed long tenure matters.

sentences.zh: 戎職在論道，吾所崇委，其解禁止。

translations.literal: Rong's duty is discussing principle—what I esteem and entrust—therefore lift the prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wang Rong counsels on the Way—a charge I prize—so I reject the impeachment.

sentences.zh: 」御史中丞解結以咸劾戎為違典制，越局侵官，干非其分，奏免咸官。

translations.literal: " Imperial Clerk Xie Jie argued Xian's impeachment of Rong breached statutes—overstepping bureau lines and meddling beyond rank—and memorialized stripping Xian's office.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Clerk Xie Jie replied that indicting Wang Rong violated jurisdiction—Fu Xian must be cashiered.

sentences.zh: 詔亦不許。

translations.literal: The edict refused again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused that too.

sentences.zh: 咸上事以為「按令，御史中丞督司百僚。

translations.literal: Xian submitted a memorial arguing: "According to statute, the Imperial Clerk supervises and regulates the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian argued: "The code charges the Imperial Clerk with oversight of every official.

sentences.zh: 皇太子以下，其在行馬內，有違法憲者皆彈糾之。

translations.literal: Below the heir apparent—those within the palace cordon—whoever violates the statutes must be impeached and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone from the crown prince downward inside the palace barriers who breaks the law falls under impeachment.

sentences.zh: 雖在行馬外，而監司不糾，亦得奏之。

translations.literal: Although outside the cordon, if supervising offices fail to correct wrongdoing, one may still memorialize them.
translations.idiomatic: Even beyond those barriers, if inspectors neglect their duty, the censor may still bring charges.

sentences.zh: 如令之文，行馬之內有違法憲，謂禁防之事耳。

translations.literal: As the ordinance reads, violations inside the cordon refer solely to palace security matters.
translations.idiomatic: The statute treats offenses inside the cordon as matters of interior palace security.

sentences.zh: 宮內禁防，外司不得而行，故專施中丞。

translations.literal: Inner-palace security may not be exercised by outer bureaus; therefore authority rests solely with the Imperial Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Outside agencies cannot police the palace interior, so the Imperial Clerk holds that jurisdiction alone.

sentences.zh: 今道路橋梁不修，鬥訟屠沽不絕，如此之比，中丞推責州坐，即今所謂行馬內語施於禁防。

translations.literal: Now roads and bridges go unrepaired; brawls, lawsuits, butchers, and vendors never cease—cases of this sort are pushed by the Imperial Clerk onto the provinces as liabilities, applying today's so-called cordon language to security enforcement.
translations.idiomatic: When bridges crumble and markets breed endless lawsuits, the censor rightly shifts blame to regional authorities—stretching "interior cordon" language to cover real governance failures.

sentences.zh: 既雲中丞督司百僚矣，何復說行馬之內乎！

translations.literal: Since the text says the Imperial Clerk oversees every official, why harp again on "inside the cordon"?
translations.idiomatic: If the censor supervises all bureaucrats, repeating "within the cordon" makes no sense.

sentences.zh: 既雲百僚，而不得復說行馬之內者，內外眾官謂之百僚，則通內外矣。

translations.literal: Once it speaks of the hundred officials it cannot again restrict meaning to the cordon—the hundred officials embrace inner and outer posts alike, comprehending both zones.
translations.idiomatic: "All officials" means capital and provincial servants together; the boundary collapses.

sentences.zh: 司隸所以不復說行馬內外者，禁防之事已於中丞說之故也。

translations.literal: The Metropolitan Governor does not repeat inner or outer cordon language because security duties were already assigned to the Imperial Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The Metropolitan Governor omits cordon wording simply because palace security belongs to the Imperial Clerk.

sentences.zh: 中丞、司隸俱糾皇太子以下，則共對司內外矣，不為中丞專司內百僚，司隸專司外百僚。

translations.literal: Imperial Clerk and Metropolitan Governor alike impeach everyone below the heir apparent—they jointly oversee inner and outer courts; the Imperial Clerk does not monopolize inner officials nor the Metropolitan Governor outer ones.
translations.idiomatic: Both officers indict everyone below the crown prince and share jurisdiction; neither is boxed into "inner" or "outer" alone.

sentences.zh: 自有中丞、司隸以來，更互奏內外眾官，惟所糾得無內外之限也。

translations.literal: Since both posts existed they have alternately memorialized inner and outer officials—whatever merits impeachment knows no cordon limit.
translations.idiomatic: Historically both offices have crossed palace walls when pressing charges; impeachment admits no artificial divide.

sentences.zh: 而結一旦橫挫臣，臣前所以不羅縷者，冀因結奏得從私願也。

translations.literal: Yet Jie suddenly humiliates your servant; the reason I earlier refrained from tedious detail was hoping his memorial might satisfy my private wish.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jie's abrupt attack surprised me; I had stayed concise hoping his complaint would let me resign quietly.

sentences.zh: 今既所願不從，而敕雲但為過耳，非所不及也，以此見原。

translations.literal: Now that my wish goes unheeded yet the edict calls it mere fault—not beyond reach—and forgives on that basis.
translations.idiomatic: My request was denied yet the throne dismisses it as a minor slip I could not help—pardoning me anyway.

sentences.zh: 臣忝司直之任，宜當正己率人，若其有過，不敢受原，是以申陳其愚。

translations.literal: Your servant disgraces the office charged with rectitude; he must straighten himself and lead others—if fault exists he dare not accept pardon—therefore lays out this foolish candor.
translations.idiomatic: As chief rectifier I must model integrity; if I erred I cannot accept blanket forgiveness—hence this blunt appeal.

sentences.zh: 司隸與中丞俱共糾皇太子以下，則從皇太子以下無所不糾也。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Governor and Imperial Clerk jointly impeach everyone below the heir apparent—therefore from that level downward nothing lies beyond impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Because both offices indict all ranks below the crown prince, no official escapes scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 得糾皇太子而不得糾尚書，臣之暗塞既所未譬。

translations.literal: Able to impeach the heir apparent yet unable to impeach the Masters of Writing—your servant's dull obstruction has never seen parallel.
translations.idiomatic: Indicting the crown prince yet barred from the Secretariat strikes me as incomprehensible.

sentences.zh: 皇太子為在行馬之內邪，皇太子在行馬之內而得糾之，尚書在行馬之內而不得糾，無有此理。

translations.literal: Is the heir apparent deemed inside the cordon? If inside yet impeachable while the Masters of Writing inside are not—no such logic exists.
translations.idiomatic: Either both crown prince and Secretariat sit inside the cordon or they do not—you cannot impeach one and shield the other.

sentences.zh: 此理灼然，而結以此挫臣。

translations.literal: This principle blazes clear—yet Jie uses it to humiliate your servant.
translations.idiomatic: The logic is obvious—yet Xie Jie twists it to shame me.

sentences.zh: 臣可無恨耳，其於觀聽，無乃有怪邪！

translations.literal: Your servant may harbor no grudge—but for those who watch and listen—is it not bizarre!
translations.idiomatic: I may swallow pride—but does the court think observers will not find this absurd?

sentences.zh: 臣識石公前在殿上脫衣，為司隸荀愷所奏，先帝不以為非，于時莫謂侵官；

translations.literal: Your servant recalls Lord Shi once removed his robe in the hall and Metropolitan Governor Xun Kai impeached him—late emperor deemed it no offense and none called it overreach.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Shi stripped his robe in court; Xun Kai charged him yet the late emperor approved—nobody cried jurisdictional trespass.

sentences.zh: 今臣裁糾尚書，而當有罪乎？

translations.literal: Now your servant merely impeaches the Masters of Writing—must that be criminal?
translations.idiomatic: Am I now guilty for indicting the Secretariat?

sentences.zh: 」咸累自上稱引故事，條理灼然，朝廷無以易之。

translations.literal: Xian repeatedly memorialized citing precedent; his clauses were lucid and the court could not refute them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian piled precedent upon precedent until the government had no answer.

sentences.zh: 吳郡顧榮常與親故書曰：「傅長虞為司隸，勁直忠果，劾按驚人。

translations.literal: Gu Rong of Wu commandery often wrote kinsmen and friends: "Fu Changyu as Metropolitan Governor—unyielding, loyal, decisive—his impeachments astonish.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong of Wu told friends: "Fu Xian as censor combines iron backbone with fearless indictments."

sentences.zh: 雖非周才，偏亮可貴也。

translations.literal: Though not a universal talent, his focused brilliance is precious.
translations.idiomatic: He may lack every virtue, yet this stubborn brilliance is priceless.

sentences.zh: 」卒官，時年五十六，詔贈司隸校尉，朝服一具、衣一襲、錢二十萬，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He died in office at fifty-six; an edict posthumously awarded Metropolitan Governor rank, one court robe, one suit, two hundred thousand cash, posthumous epithet Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died on duty at fifty-six with posthumous honors as Metropolitan Governor, burial vestments, cash, and the epithet "Steadfast."

sentences.zh: 有三子：敷、晞、纂。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Fu, Xi, and Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Fu Fu, Fu Xi, and Fu Zuan.

sentences.zh: 長子敷嗣。

translations.literal: Eldest son Fu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest, Fu Fu, inherited his rank.

sentences.zh: 敷字穎根，清靜有道，素解屬文。

translations.literal: Fu, courtesy name Yingen, was quiet and principled and naturally skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Fu, courtesy name Yingen, lived plainly, cultivated the Way, and wrote with ease.

sentences.zh: 除太子舍人，轉尚書郎、太傅參軍，皆不起。

translations.literal: He was appointed Heir Apparent Household Gentleman, transferred to Masters of Writing Gentleman and Grand Tutor army adviser—all posts he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Court posts as tutor, Secretariat aide, and army adviser came his way; he refused each.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之亂，避地會稽，元帝引為鎮東從事中郎。

translations.literal: During the Yongjia upheaval he fled to Kuaiji; Prince Yuan of Langya summoned him as staff supervisor to the east-stabilizing general.
translations.idiomatic: When chaos erupted in Yongjia he took refuge in Kuaiji; the future Yuan Emperor named him aide on the eastern headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 素有贏疾，頻見敦喻，辭不獲免，輿病到職。

translations.literal: Always consumptive, repeatedly urged by earnest instruction, unable to escape refusal—he was carried ill to assume duty.
translations.idiomatic: Chronic illness notwithstanding, repeated summons forced him to take the post carried on a litter.

sentences.zh: 數月卒，時年四十六。

translations.literal: After several months he died, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died within months, forty-six years old.

sentences.zh: 晞亦有才思，為上虞令，甚有政績，卒于司徒西曹屬。

translations.literal: Xi also possessed literary talent; as magistrate of Shangyu he achieved notable administration; he died as Western Bureau clerk under the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xi wrote well, governed Shangyu with distinction, and ended his career in the Minister of Education's western bureau.

sentences.zh: 傅祗

translations.literal: Fu Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi is treated in the following biography.

sentences.zh: 祗字子莊。

translations.literal: Zhi, courtesy name Zizhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi's courtesy name was Zizhuang.

sentences.zh: 父嘏，魏太常。

translations.literal: His father Fu Jia was Wei Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fu Jia had served Wei as Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 祗性至孝，早知名，以才識明練稱。

translations.literal: Zhi was supremely filial by nature, became known early, and was praised for talent, judgment, and administrative polish.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned from youth for filial devotion, he earned esteem as a capable and seasoned administrator.

sentences.zh: 武帝始建東宮，起家太子舍人，累遷散騎黃門郎，賜爵關內侯，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu first founded the Eastern Palace he rose as Heir Apparent Household Gentleman, repeatedly promoted to Cavalry Attendant and Gentleman at Yellow Gates, ennobled marquis within the passes with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's creation of the heir's establishment launched Fu Zhi's career; he climbed to palace attendant posts and received a marquis title over three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職。

translations.literal: Mother's mourning removed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 及葬母，詔給太常五等吉凶導從。

translations.literal: When burying his mother an edict supplied the Grand Master of Ceremonies with five-grade auspicious and inauspicious escorts.
translations.idiomatic: For her burial the court assigned the Ministry of Rites full honor guards for both ritual segments.

sentences.zh: 其後諸卿夫人葬給導從，自此始也。

translations.literal: Afterward ministers' wives received escorts at burial—beginning here.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth elite wives won the same cortège privilege.

sentences.zh: 服終，為滎陽太守。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he became Administrator of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he took charge of Xingyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 自魏黃初大水之後，河濟泛溢，鄧艾嘗著《濟河論》，開石門而通之，至是復浸壞。

translations.literal: Since Wei's Huangchu floods the Yellow River and Ji had spilled; Deng Ai once wrote the Discourse on the Ji River, cutting Stone Gate to channel them—by now works again silted and broke.
translations.idiomatic: After Huangchu-era inundations Deng Ai had dredged the Ji through Stone Gate; those defenses again collapsed under Fu Zhi's watch.

sentences.zh: 祗乃造沈萊堰，至今兗、豫無水患，百姓為立碑頌焉。

translations.literal: Zhi then built the Shenlai weir; to this day Yan and Yu suffer no flood disasters—the people erected a stele praising him.
translations.idiomatic: His Shenlai weir shielded Yan and Yu from floods and earned a popular monument.

sentences.zh: 尋表兼廷尉，遷常侍、左軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon memorialized concurrent Commandant of Justice; promoted Regular Palace Attendant and General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: He added chief judgeship, then rose to palace attendant and commander of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，梓宮在殯，而太傅楊駿輔政，欲悅眾心，議普進封爵。

translations.literal: When the emperor died and the coffin lay in mourning, Grand Tutor Yang Jun directed government and sought to please the multitude by debating blanket advancement of noble ranks.
translations.idiomatic: During the lying-in-state Yang Jun courted popularity by proposing wholesale noble promotions.

sentences.zh: 祗與駿書曰：「未有帝王始崩，臣下論功者也。

translations.literal: Zhi wrote Jun: "Never has an emperor just died while ministers tally merit.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi wrote Yang Jun: "Ministers do not divide spoils while the sovereign still lies unburied.

sentences.zh: 」駿不從。

translations.literal: Jun did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun ignored him.

sentences.zh: 入為侍中。

translations.literal: He entered court as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Palace Attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 時將誅駿，而駿不之知。

translations.literal: At the moment Jun was to be executed—yet Jun did not know.
translations.idiomatic: The coup against Yang Jun was imminent while he remained oblivious.

sentences.zh: 祗侍駿坐，而雲龍門閉，內外不通。

translations.literal: Zhi attended Jun seated—yet Cloud Dragon Gate closed and inner and outer could not communicate.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi sat with Yang Jun while Cloud Dragon Gate slammed shut, severing palace traffic.

sentences.zh: 祗請與尚書武茂聽國家消息，揖而下階。

translations.literal: Zhi requested with Masters of Writing Wu Mao to hear state tidings—bowed and descended steps.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi bowed to Wu Mao of the Secretariat and urged him outside for news.

sentences.zh: 茂猶坐，祗顧曰：「君非天子臣邪！

translations.literal: Mao still sat; Zhi looked saying: "Are you not the Son of Heaven's minister!
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mao lingered; Fu Zhi snapped, "Are you not the emperor's servant?

sentences.zh: 今內外隔絕，不知國家所在，何得安坐！

translations.literal: Now inner and outer are cut off—we do not know where the state stands—how can you sit at ease!
translations.idiomatic: Couriers cannot pass yet you lounge here clueless about the realm!

sentences.zh: 」茂乃驚起。

translations.literal: Mao then startled and rose.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mao jumped up in alarm.

sentences.zh: 駿既伏誅，裴楷息瓚，駿之婿也，為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: Jun having been executed, Pei Kai's son Zan—Jun's son-in-law—was killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Jun died, his son-in-law Pei Zan fell to rampaging soldiers.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射荀愷與楷不平，因奏楷是駿親，收付廷尉。

translations.literal: Left Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Xun Kai bore Pei Kai ill—thereby memorialized Kai was Jun kin—arrested and handed to Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Kai, nursing a grudge against Pei Kai, denounced him as Yang Jun's kinsman and had him jailed.

sentences.zh: 祗證楷無罪，有詔赦之。

translations.literal: Zhi testified Kai had no crime—an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi vouched for Pei Kai's innocence and won an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 時又收駿官屬，祗復啟曰：「昔魯芝為曹爽司馬，斬關出赴爽，宣帝義之，尚遷青州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time Jun's staff were also seized; Zhi again submitted: "Formerly Lu Zhi was Cao Shuang's Major—cut gate bolts to reach Shuang—Emperor Xuan deemed it righteous—still promoted Qingzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jun's aides were rounded up Fu Zhi cited Lu Zhi, whom Emperor Sima Yi honored despite rushing to Cao Shuang's doomed camp.

sentences.zh: 駿之僚佐不可加罰。

translations.literal: Jun's aides must not receive added punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun's clerks deserve no extra penalties.

sentences.zh: 」詔又赦之。

translations.literal: An edict again pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict freed them.

sentences.zh: 祗多所維正皆如此。

translations.literal: Zhi's many upholdings of rectitude were all like this.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi repeatedly steadied justice in just this fashion.

sentences.zh: 除河南尹，未拜，遷司隸校尉。

translations.literal: Appointed Administrator of Henan—not invested—transferred Metropolitan Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Named to Henan but promoted Metropolitan Governor before taking office.

sentences.zh: 以討楊駿勳，當封郡公八千戶，固讓，減半，降封靈川縣公，千八百戶，餘二千二百戶封少子暢為武鄉亭侯。

translations.literal: For merit punishing Yang Jun he should have been enfeoffed commandery duke eight thousand households—firmly declined—halved—reduced to county duke of Lingchuan with one thousand eight hundred households—the remaining two thousand two hundred enfeoffed youngest son Chang as village marquis of Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His reward for crushing Yang Jun should have been an eight-thousand-household duchy; after demurring he accepted a smaller county duchy and split stipends to son Fu Chang.

sentences.zh: 又以本封賜兄子雋為東明亭侯。

translations.literal: Also with original fief gifted elder brother's son Jun as village marquis of Dongming.
translations.idiomatic: He further assigned part of his fief to nephew Fu Jun as eastern village marquis.

sentences.zh: 楚王瑋之矯詔也，祗以聞奏稽留，免官。

translations.literal: When Prince of Chu Wei forged an edict—Zhi because memorial reporting was delayed—stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Wei's false edict caught Fu Zhi slow to report; he lost his post.

sentences.zh: 期年，遷光祿勳，復以公事免。

translations.literal: Full year—promoted Superintendent of the Imperial Household—again dismissed over public affair.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he headed the household ministry yet another bureaucratic spat ended the job.

sentences.zh: 氐人齊萬年舉兵反，以祗為行安西軍司，加常侍，率安西將軍夏侯駿討平之。

translations.literal: The Di leader Qi Wannian raised troops in rebellion—appointed Zhi acting army director for west-pacifying—added Regular Attendant—led General Who Pacifies the West Xiahou Jun to crush and pacify.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Wannian rebelled Fu Zhi served as acting chief of staff on the western expedition alongside General Xiahou Jun.

sentences.zh: 遷衛尉，以風疾遜位，就拜常侍，食卿祿秩，賜錢及床帳等。
