translations.literal: Promoted Defender-in-Chief—because wind illness yielded position—thereupon appointed Regular Attendant—ate minister salary ranks—gifted cash and bedding curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Defender-in-Chief briefly—then palsy forced retirement with attendant stipends, cash, and furnishings.

sentences.zh: 尋加光祿大夫，門施行馬。

translations.literal: Soon added Grand Counsellor—gate applied traveling horse barriers.
translations.idiomatic: He gained Grand Counsellor rank and cordoned carriage lanes before his gate.

sentences.zh: 及趙王倫輔政，以為中書監，常侍如故，以鎮眾心。

translations.literal: When Prince of Zhao Lun assisted governance—appointed Director of Palace Secretariat—Regular Attendant as before—to pacify crowd hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Lun's regency named him Palace Secretariat director to calm opinion.

sentences.zh: 祗辭之以疾，倫遣御史輿祗就職。

translations.literal: Zhi declined citing illness—Lun dispatched Imperial Clerk carrying Zhi to assume office.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded sickness; Sima Lun sent clerks to haul him to his desk.

sentences.zh: 王戎、陳准等相與言曰：「傅公在事，吾屬無憂矣。

translations.literal: Wang Rong and Chen Zhun mutually said: "Lord Fu handling affairs—we group no worry.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong and Chen Zhun agreed: "With Lord Fu in charge we may breathe easy.

sentences.zh: 」其為物所倚信如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he relied on by the world.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the confidence peers placed in him.

sentences.zh: 倫篡，又為右光祿、開府，加侍中。

translations.literal: Lun usurped—again became Right Grand Counsellor, establish office—added Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Lun seized the throne Fu Zhi rose to Right Grand Counsellor with independent headquarters and a palace seat.

sentences.zh: 惠帝還宮，祗以經受偽職請退，不許。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui returned palace—Zhi because he underwent false posts requested retirement—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui's restoration brought requests to resign tainted posts; the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 初，倫之篡也，孫秀與義陽王威等十餘人預撰儀式禪文。

translations.literal: Earlier—Lun's usurpation—Sun Xiu with Prince of Yiyang Wei and ten-plus others beforehand drafted ritual abdication texts.
translations.idiomatic: During Sima Lun's coup Sun Xiu and Prince Sima Wei pre-drafted abdication liturgy.

sentences.zh: 及倫敗，齊王冏收侍中劉逵、常侍騶捷、杜育、黃門郎陸機、右丞周導、王尊等付廷尉。

translations.literal: When Lun fell—Prince of Qi Jiong arrested Palace Attendant Liu Kui—Regular Attendants Zou Jie and Du Yu—Gentleman at Yellow Gates Lu Ji—Right Assistant Director Zhou Dao and Wang Zun etc.—handed to Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun's fall led Prince Sima Jiong to jail Liu Kui, Zou Jie, Du Yu, Lu Ji, Zhou Dao, Wang Zun, and others.

sentences.zh: 以禪文出中書，復議處祗罪，會赦得原。

translations.literal: Because abdication text issued from Palace Secretariat—again debated punishing Zhi crime—met amnesty obtained pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Because the abdication edict came from his bureau he faced renewed charges until an amnesty intervened.

sentences.zh: 後以禪文草本非祗所撰，於是詔復光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later because abdication text draft was not composed by Zhi—thereupon edict restored Grand Counsellor.
translations.idiomatic: Investigators learned he never drafted the abdication scrap; his Grand Counsellor rank returned.

sentences.zh: 子宣，尚弘農公主。

translations.literal: Son Xuan—married Princess of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu Xuan wed the Princess of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太子少傅，上章遜位還第。

translations.literal: Soon promoted Junior Tutor to heir apparent—submitted memorial yielding position returning mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Tutor followed soon after, then memorialized to retire home.

sentences.zh: 及成都王穎為太傅，復以祗為少傅，加侍中。

translations.literal: When Prince of Chengdu Ying became Grand Tutor—again appointed Zhi Junior Tutor—added Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Ying's grand tutorship recalled Fu Zhi as junior tutor with palace status.

sentences.zh: 懷帝即位，遷光祿大夫、侍中，未拜，加右僕射、中書監。

translations.literal: Emperor Huai ascended—promoted Grand Counsellor, Palace Attendant—not invested—added Right Supervisor, Director of Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai stacked honors on him—Grand Counsellor, palace attendant, Right Vice-President, and Secretariat director—before investiture caught up.

sentences.zh: 時太傅東海王越輔政，祗既居端右，每宣君臣謙光之道，由此上下雍穆。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Tutor Prince of Donghai Yue assisted governance—Zhi already occupied summit right—every proclaimed lord-minister modest radiant Way—thereby above below harmonious reverent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Prince Sima Yue's regency Fu Zhi preached humility between sovereign and ministers, easing court tensions.

sentences.zh: 祗明達國體，朝廷制度多所經綜。

translations.literal: Zhi clearly comprehended state body—court institutions much managed synthesized.
translations.idiomatic: His grasp of state protocol let him harmonize sprawling regulations.

sentences.zh: 曆左光祿、開府，行太子太傅，侍中如故。

translations.literal: Passed Left Grand Counsellor, establish office—acting Grand Tutor to heir apparent—Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He rotated through Left Grand Counsellor with independent staff, acted as heir's grand tutor, and kept palace attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 疾篤遜位，不許。

translations.literal: Illness severe yielded position—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Terminal illness could not win retirement approval.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒，以足疾，詔版輿上殿，不拜。

translations.literal: Promoted Minister of Education—because foot illness—edict palanquin ascend hall—not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Made Minister of Education despite lameness—porters carried him to audience exempt from bows.

sentences.zh: 大將軍苟晞表請遷都，使祗出詣河陰，修理舟楫，為水行之備。

translations.literal: General-in-Chief Gou Xi memorialized requesting moving capital—ordered Zhi go out to Heyin—repair boats and oars—as preparation for water travel.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi's plan to relocate the court sent Fu Zhi to Heyin to ready boats.

sentences.zh: 及洛陽陷沒，遂共建行台，推祗為盟主，以司徒、持節、大都督諸軍事傳檄四方。

translations.literal: When Luoyang fell submerged—thereupon jointly erected mobile headquarters—promoted Zhi alliance leader—with Minister of Education, credential, grand area commander all military affairs—spread proclamations four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's fall spawned a field headquarters headed by Fu Zhi as covenant chief with full military credentials.

sentences.zh: 遣子宣將公主與尚書令和郁赴告方伯征義兵，祗自屯盟津小城，宣弟暢行河陰令，以待宣。

translations.literal: Dispatched son Xuan leading princess with Masters of Writing Director He Yu go notify regional governors summon righteous troops—Zhi self garrisoned Mengjin minor city—Xuan's younger brother Chang acting Heyin magistrate—to await Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan escorted the princess with He Yu to rally provincial armies while Fu Zhi held Mengjin and Fu Chang acted as Heyin magistrate pending their return.

sentences.zh: 祗以暴疾薨，時年六十九。

translations.literal: Zhi by sudden illness died—aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: A violent illness killed him at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 祗自以義誠不終，力疾手筆敕厲其二子宣、暢，辭旨深切，覽者莫不感激慷慨。

translations.literal: Zhi self deemed righteousness sincerity not completed—with force illness hand wrote instruct exhort his two sons Xuan Chang—word intent deep cutting—viewers none not stirred generous.
translations.idiomatic: Believing his loyal mission unfinished, he scribbled fierce counsel to Fu Xuan and Fu Chang—words so poignant readers wept.

sentences.zh: 祗著文章駁論十餘萬言。

translations.literal: Zhi composed essays refuting discourse exceeding hundred thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: His polemical writings exceeded one hundred thousand characters.

sentences.zh: 宣字世弘。

translations.literal: Xuan courtesy name Shihong.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan's courtesy name was Shihong.

sentences.zh: 年六歲喪繼母，哭泣如成人，中表異之。

translations.literal: Age six lost stepmother—weeping like adult—cousins marveled.
translations.idiomatic: At six he mourned his stepmother like a grown man—kinsfolk were astonished.

sentences.zh: 及長，好學，趙王倫以為相國掾、尚書郎、太子中舍人，遷司徒西曹掾。

translations.literal: When grown—loved learning—Prince of Zhao Lun appointed him aide to minister of state, Masters of Writing Gentleman, Household Gentleman of heir apparent—promoted Western Bureau aide under Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Adult studies brought posts under Prince Sima Lun—ministerial aide, Secretariat gentleman, heir's adviser—then western bureau clerk.

sentences.zh: 去職，累遷為秘書丞、驃騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: Left office—repeatedly promoted to Assistant Director of Palace Library, Staff Supervisor to Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: After quitting earlier posts he rose to library deputy and champion-general aide.

sentences.zh: 惠帝至自長安，以宣為左丞，不就，遷黃門郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui arrived from Chang'an—appointed Xuan Left Assistant Director—did not take up—promoted Gentleman at Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui's return from Chang'an offered Fu Xuan the left assistant directorship; he declined but accepted a Yellow Gates post.

sentences.zh: 懷帝即位，轉吏部郎，又為御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended he transferred to Personnel Gentleman and again became Imperial Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai shifted him into the Ministry of Personnel and restored him as Imperial Clerk.

sentences.zh: 卒年四十九，無子，以暢子沖為嗣。

translations.literal: He died at forty-nine—without son—made Chang's son Chong heir.
translations.idiomatic: Childless at forty-nine, he adopted nephew Fu Chong, Fu Chang's son, as successor.

sentences.zh: 暢字世道。

translations.literal: Chang, courtesy name Shidao.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chang used the courtesy name Shidao.

sentences.zh: 年五歲，父友見而戲之，解暢衣，取其金環與侍者，暢不之惜，以此賞之。

translations.literal: At age five a father's friend saw him and teased him—removed Chang's clothes—took his gold ring giving it to an attendant—Chang did not regret it—thereby they praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was five a friend of his father stripped him in jest and handed his gold ring to a servant; Fu Chang scarcely cared—earning adult admiration.

sentences.zh: 年未弱冠，甚有重名。

translations.literal: Years not yet weak cap—very had heavy reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Before his capping ceremony he already enjoyed wide renown.

sentences.zh: 以選入侍講東宮，為秘書丞。

translations.literal: By selection entered lecturing Eastern Palace—became Assistant Director of Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen to lecture in the heir's palace, he served as deputy director of the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 尋沒于石勒，勒以為大將軍右司馬。

translations.literal: Soon fell captive to Shi Le—Le appointed him Major on the Right for the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Captured by Shi Le, he became senior aide on the latter's general staff.

sentences.zh: 諳識朝儀，恆居機密，勒甚重之。

translations.literal: Thoroughly knew court ritual—always dwelt in secrets—Le greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Fluent in court etiquette and privy to military secrets, he won Shi Le's deep respect.

sentences.zh: 作《晉諸公敘贊》二十二卷，又為《公卿故事》九卷。

translations.literal: He composed twenty-two fascicles of Narrative Encomia for Jin Grandees (Jin zhugong xu zan) and nine fascicles of Tales of Dukes and Ministers (Gongqing gushi).
translations.idiomatic: His literary legacy includes twenty-two scrolls of encomiastic sketches on Jin statesmen and nine scrolls of anecdotes about high ministers.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: His life came to an end.

sentences.zh: 子詠，過江為交州刺史、太子右率。

translations.literal: Son Yong—crossed the Yangzi to become Inspector of Jiaozhou and Right Leader for the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu Yong crossed south to serve as Jiaozhou inspector and commander of the heir's right guard.

sentences.zh: 【史評】

translations.literal: [Historians' appraisal]
translations.idiomatic: Historians' appraisal.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：武帝覽觀四方，平章百姓，永言啟沃，任切爭臣。

translations.literal: The historians say: Emperor Wu surveyed the four quarters and harmonized the hundred clans—ever seeking fruitful counsel—and urgently entrusted contentious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The chroniclers observe that Emperor Wu toured the realm, settled the people, thirsted for blunt advice, and leaned heavily on remonstrating officials.

sentences.zh: 傅玄體強直之姿，懷匪躬之操，抗辭正色，補闕弼違，諤諤當朝，不忝其職者矣。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan embodied rigid uprightness—cherished selfless integrity—argued with stern demeanor—remedied omissions and corrected faults—spoke bluntly at court—and did not disgrace his office.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan united moral backbone with fearless counsel, plugging policy gaps and exposing wrongdoing—he honored every charge the throne gave him.

sentences.zh: 及乎位居三獨，彈擊是司，遂能使台閣生風，貴戚斂手。

translations.literal: Once he occupied one of the three independent posts—impeachment being his charge—he could make the ministries chill with awe and noble kin clasp their hands.
translations.idiomatic: Heading an autonomous censorate he froze the bureaucracy with indictments and cowed powerful families.

sentences.zh: 雖前代鮑、葛，何以加之！

translations.literal: Even Bao and Ge of former ages—what could surpass him!
translations.idiomatic: Not even Han exemplars such as Bao Xuan and Ge Yi clearly outshone him!

sentences.zh: 然而惟此褊心，乏弘雅之度，驟聞競爽，為物議所譏，惜哉！

translations.literal: Yet only this narrow heart—lacked vast refined measure—rash contention for superiority—was mocked by worldly opinion—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Yet his cramped temper lacked gracious breadth; quick quarrels drew public sneers—a pity!

sentences.zh: 古人取戒于韋弦，良有以也。

translations.literal: The ancients took warning from leather and bowstring—truly there was reason.
translations.idiomatic: The classical metaphor of soft leather versus tight bowstring warns temperaments like his—and aptly so.

sentences.zh: 長虞風格凝峻，弗墜家聲。

translations.literal: Changyu's manner was austere and stern—did not drop family renown.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian's icy dignity preserved the Fu family's reputation.

sentences.zh: 及其納諫汝南，獻書臨晉，居諒直之地，有先見之明矣。

translations.literal: As to his accepting remonstrance from Runan—presenting writings at Linjin—dwelling in candid integrity—he possessed prescience.
translations.idiomatic: His blunt counsel to Prince Liang of Runan and timely memorials at Linjin showed principled foresight.

sentences.zh: 傅祗名父之子，早樹風猷，崎嶇危亂之朝，匡救君臣之際，卒能保全祿位，可謂有道存焉。

translations.literal: Fu Zhi was a famous father's son—early established moral influence—in rugged perilous chaotic courts—aiding lord and ministers at the crisis—finally able to preserve salary and rank—may be called the Way dwelling therein.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi, heir to a celebrated father, forged his ethos young and steadied sovereign and ministers through turmoil—emerging with honor intact proves statesmanship.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：鶉觚貞諒，實惟朝望。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Chungu's steadfast sincerity—truly was the court's expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Verdict: Fu Xuan of Chungu bore unyielding integrity—the moral compass of his age.

sentences.zh: 志厲強直，性乖夷曠。

translations.literal: Aspiration fierce and rigid—nature contrary to easy openness.
translations.idiomatic: His will demanded blunt honor yet his temper refused mellow ease.

sentences.zh: 長虞剛簡，無虧風尚。

translations.literal: Changyu stern and spare—without losing moral fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian's austerity never betrayed public virtue.

sentences.zh: 子莊才識，爰膺袞職。

translations.literal: Zizhuang's talent and judgment—thereupon bore ceremonial-robe office.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi's abilities earned him ministerial robes and key portfolios.

sentences.zh: 忠績未申，泉途遽逼。

translations.literal: Loyal deeds not declared—spring road hastily pressed.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal service unfinished—death closed in overnight.

translations.literal: The received text records only an equals sign without lexical meaning.
translations.idiomatic: No interpretable Chinese sentence survives in this lemma.

translations.literal: Another stray equals sign appears without readable words.
translations.idiomatic: Another transcription artifact yields no translatable clause.
